---
title: "xenium_nb — QC"
subtitle: "Per-sample QC before clustering, and the filtering thresholds it implies"
# Pin the kernel by name, as cluster_report.qmd does. Apptainer bind-mounts $HOME, so
# kernelspecs from ~/.local/share/jupyter/kernels shadow the container's own — quarto's
# default "python3" then resolves to a host env missing the pipeline's packages, and
# every cell fails at import under `error: true` while the render still exits 0.
jupyter: python_spatial
format:
  pptx:
    reference-doc: ouhsc_ppt_template.pptx
    # `#` becomes a Section Header slide, `##` a Title-and-Content slide. Without
    # this pandoc infers the level from the headings present, so adding the first
    # `#` would silently demote every `##` to a bullet.
    slide-level: 2
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  # Keep rendering when a cell raises: one sample's panel erroring leaves an error slide
  # in its own section instead of taking the whole deck down. The cost is that a
  # genuinely broken cell yields an error slide and an exit code of 0 — read the slides,
  # not just the exit status.
  error: true
---

```{python}
# | tags: [setup]
import traceback
from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import zarr
from IPython.display import display, Markdown
from matplotlib.colors import LogNorm

# The reference template is 16:9 at 10 x 5.625in; leave room for a slide title.
FIGSIZE = (9.0, 4.3)
# Inches reserved beside the in-tissue plots for their colorbar, which sits outside
# the axes and would otherwise be cropped by tight_layout.
LEGEND_WIDTH = 1.4
# Fraction of the in-tissue axes the cell dots should cover, which sets their size.
SPATIAL_COVERAGE = 0.45

# Every raw zarr is staged into this notebook's working directory by the Nextflow
# process, so globbing is the whole input contract — no params to pass or drift.
#
# These are create_sdata's zarrs, NOT cluster_sdata's: nothing here has been filtered
# yet, which is the point. Reading this deck off clustered zarrs would show the
# distributions that survived the very cut the deck exists to choose, with the discarded
# tail already gone — every threshold would then look harmless.
ZARRS = sorted(Path(".").glob("*.zarr"))
if not ZARRS:
    raise FileNotFoundError("No .zarr directories staged next to the notebook.")

# The thresholds cluster_sdata* apply today, and what the emitted qc_thresholds.csv is
# pre-filled with. They are drawn on the retention slides as a reference line so each
# sample's curve is read against the cut currently in force, not against nothing.
DEFAULT_MIN_COUNTS = 10
DEFAULT_MIN_CELLS = 5

# Thresholds the retention curves are evaluated at. Dense where the decision actually
# sits (a Xenium cell with under ~50 transcripts is mostly noise) and sparse above it,
# since the curve is flat there and only the shape matters.
COUNT_GRID = np.array([0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200])
# The per-gene equivalent. A targeted panel is curated, so the interesting range is
# small — genes detected in single-digit numbers of cells are the only ones at risk.
CELL_GRID = np.array([0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100])

# The count thresholds called out in the retention table on each sample's slide. A
# subset of COUNT_GRID: the curve shows the shape, the table gives numbers to quote.
COUNT_CALLOUTS = [5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100]

# The per-cell QC columns each sample's distribution panel shows, as
# (obs column, axis label, log scale).
#
# All four come straight from the zarr — create_sdata annotates the transcript and gene
# counts, and the Xenium reader supplies both areas from cells.parquet. This deck derives
# no QC of its own beyond the negative-control fraction below, which has no home upstream
# yet.
QC_COLUMNS = [
    ("transcript_counts", "Transcripts per cell", True),
    ("n_genes_by_transcripts", "Genes per cell", True),
    ("cell_area", "Cell area (µm²)", True),
    ("nucleus_area", "Nucleus area (µm²)", True),
]

# obs columns holding the five Xenium control/codeword counters, as the reader writes
# them. Summed for the negative-control panel — each alone is far too sparse to read.
CONTROL_COLS = [
    "control_probe_counts",
    "genomic_control_counts",
    "control_codeword_counts",
    "unassigned_codeword_counts",
    "deprecated_codeword_counts",
]

# Every obs column this deck reads, checked up front in load_sample. All of them come
# from create_sdata or the Xenium reader; none is derived here. Listing them in one
# place means a zarr that predates a column fails on the first sample with the column
# named, rather than several slides later inside whichever panel happened to want it.
REQUIRED_OBS = (
    [col for col, _, _ in QC_COLUMNS]
    + CONTROL_COLS
    + ["control_counts", "pct_control", "segmentation_method", "sample"]
)


def load_sample(path):
    """Read one zarr's obs, var, and spatial coords without pulling X into memory.

    ad.io.read_elem on the table's zarr groups reads obs/var/obsm only — the count matrix
    stays on disk, and this deck never needs it. Every metric shown is already annotated:
    create_sdata computes the per-cell and per-gene QC at the one point X is in memory
    precisely so a QC report can work from obs and var alone.

    spatialdata.read_zarr would instead materialize every image, point, and shape for
    each sample, which for a cohort of whole-slide Xenium runs is the difference between
    a deck that renders on a laptop and one that does not.
    """
    store = zarr.open(f"{path}/tables/table", mode="r")
    obs = ad.io.read_elem(store["obs"])
    var = ad.io.read_elem(store["var"])
    spatial = ad.io.read_elem(store["obsm"]["spatial"])
    obs["spatial_x"] = spatial[:, 0]
    obs["spatial_y"] = spatial[:, 1]

    # This deck computes no QC metric of its own — pct_control included, which
    # create_sdata now annotates alongside the rest. A report that derives a metric is
    # a second definition of it, and the two drift without anything saying so.
    #
    # Deliberately no fallback for zarrs predating a column: a fallback is that second
    # definition wearing a disguise, and it would let a stale cohort render a deck whose
    # numbers came from somewhere other than the pipeline. Failing here names the fix,
    # which is to re-run create_sdata.
    missing = [c for c in REQUIRED_OBS if c not in obs.columns]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(
            f"{Path(path).name}: obs is missing {missing}. These come from create_sdata "
            "— re-run it over this sample rather than deriving them here."
        )

    return obs, var


def retained_fraction(values, grid):
    """Fraction of `values` at or above each threshold in `grid`.

    Matches what scanpy's filters actually do — sc.pp.filter_cells(min_counts=n) and
    sc.pp.filter_genes(min_cells=n) both KEEP at n, so the cut is >= n, not > n. Getting
    that off by one would misreport the default cut by a whole threshold step.

    Sorting once and searching is what lets both the per-sample curves and the cohort
    overlay run over a full grid without rescanning the column per threshold.
    """
    ordered = np.sort(np.asarray(values, dtype=float))
    # searchsorted(..., "left") counts strictly-below, so the complement is the >= side.
    return 1 - np.searchsorted(ordered, grid, side="left") / len(ordered)


def log_hist(ax, values, label, log):
    """One QC distribution panel, with its median marked.

    Non-positive values are dropped from a log panel rather than silently shifting the
    whole distribution to make them plottable: transcript_counts reaches 0 on real data,
    and nucleus_area is 0 for every cell segmented without a nucleus. Both are exactly
    the cells a QC deck must not hide, so the count that fell off is printed in the panel
    title instead of being folded into the first bin.
    """
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    values = values[np.isfinite(values)]
    if log:
        positive = values[values > 0]
        n_dropped = len(values) - len(positive)
        bins = np.logspace(np.log10(positive.min()), np.log10(positive.max()), 60)
        ax.set_xscale("log")
    else:
        positive, n_dropped, bins = values, 0, 60

    ax.hist(positive, bins=bins, color="#4C72B0")
    median = float(np.median(values))
    ax.axvline(median, color="#C44E52", lw=1.2)
    ax.set_xlabel(label, size=7)
    ax.set_ylabel("Cells", size=7)
    title = f"median {median:,.0f}"
    if n_dropped:
        title += f" · {n_dropped:,} at zero"
    ax.set_title(title, size=7)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)


def point_size(ax, n_cells, coverage=SPATIAL_COVERAGE):
    """Marker area (pt²) that lets n_cells cover `coverage` of these axes, once.

    A fixed size cannot serve every tissue plot: at s=3 a 21k-cell strip reads well but a
    32k-cell section is a solid mat of dots, and at s=1 the strip is speckle. Taking the
    axes' own area covers both — get_position() is the pre-tight_layout fraction of the
    figure, close enough for a marker size. 72 pt to the inch, squared, converts inches²
    to the pt² units scatter's `s` is in.
    """
    w, h = ax.get_figure().get_size_inches()
    pos = ax.get_position()
    area_pt2 = (pos.width * w) * (pos.height * h) * 72 ** 2
    return float(np.clip(coverage * area_pt2 / n_cells, 0.5, 6.0))


def tissue_figure(obs, n):
    """A figure holding `n` tissue panels, laid out and sized to fill the slide.

    A fixed FIGSIZE wastes the slide on anything that is not 2:1: a tall section renders
    as a sliver down the middle of a wide figure, because set_aspect("equal") is
    non-negotiable for tissue. Sizing the figure to the data's aspect instead means the
    image pandoc embeds is all tissue, and PowerPoint centres it on the slide.

    The ORIENTATION has to follow the tissue too, which is why this does not just take a
    column count. These ROIs are wide strips (~3:1), and two of those side by side make a
    6:1 figure that pandoc scales to the slide width — leaving two panels about a
    centimetre tall in a band of whitespace. Stacking the same two panels gives 1.5:1,
    close to the slide's own proportions, and each panel keeps real estate. A tall tissue
    inverts the argument, so the layout is chosen per sample rather than fixed: whichever
    of the two arrangements lands closest to the slide's aspect wins, compared in log
    space so being twice too wide and half too wide count equally.
    """
    aspect = np.ptp(obs["spatial_x"]) / np.ptp(obs["spatial_y"])
    box_w, box_h = FIGSIZE[0] - LEGEND_WIDTH, FIGSIZE[1]
    target = box_w / box_h

    nrows, ncols = min([(1, n), (n, 1)],
                       key=lambda rc: abs(np.log(aspect * rc[1] / rc[0] / target)))
    combined = aspect * ncols / nrows
    # Fit the combined block inside the slide's plot box, touching whichever edge binds.
    w, h = (box_w, box_w / combined) if combined >= target else (box_h * combined, box_h)
    return plt.subplots(nrows, ncols, figsize=(w + LEGEND_WIDTH, h), squeeze=False)


def sample_colors(n):
    """n categorical colours for the cohort overlays.

    tab10 below 11 samples and tab20 above, matching cluster_report's rule. Sample
    identity is unordered, so a categorical palette that maximises adjacent contrast is
    the right kind — unlike sample_summary's cluster ramp, where adjacency carries
    meaning.
    """
    cmap = plt.get_cmap("tab10" if n <= 10 else "tab20")
    return [cmap(i % cmap.N) for i in range(n)]
```

```{python}
# One `# <sample>` section per sample, driven by the staged zarrs rather than a hardcoded
# block each: the cohort changes, and a hardcoded list silently omits a new sample while
# raising KeyError on a removed one.
#
# Each sample's obs and var are dropped as soon as its slides are drawn; only the small
# per-sample summaries the cohort section needs are carried forward, so a cohort's worth
# of obs frames is never co-resident.
#
# The headings are emitted with display(Markdown(...)) from inside an ORDINARY cell, NOT
# under `output: asis`. Under asis everything a cell displays concatenates into one raw
# markdown stream: the figure lands between the blocks and leaves the next heading not
# starting its own line, so pandoc prints a literal "## ..." as text and drops the image
# entirely. display(Markdown) does not hit it — each call emits its own complete block,
# and each figure ends with plt.show() so it lands between them.

# Carried out of the loop for the cohort section: one summary row per sample, plus the
# retention curves and the ECDF inputs the overlay slides redraw.
summaries = []
curves = {}
distributions = {}

for path in ZARRS:
    obs, var = load_sample(path)

    # obs["sample"] is written by create_sdata, so the sample id comes from the object
    # rather than the staged path — which is a meaningless sample1.zarr, since the
    # process stages every zarr under an indexed name.
    sample = str(obs["sample"].iloc[0])

    display(Markdown(f"# {sample}"))

    # One try around the whole sample. This loop is a single cell, so anything raising
    # here without being caught aborts the cell and drops every LATER sample from the
    # deck too — with the render still exiting 0 under `error: true`. Catching per sample
    # keeps the rest of the cohort. The cost is that the first failure ends this sample:
    # its section gets a traceback instead of its remaining slides.
    try:
        counts = obs["transcript_counts"].to_numpy()
        gene_cells = var["n_cells_by_transcripts"].to_numpy()
        cell_curve = retained_fraction(counts, COUNT_GRID)
        gene_curve = retained_fraction(gene_cells, CELL_GRID)

        # ── Per-cell distributions ────────────────────────────────────────────
        display(Markdown("## Per-cell QC distributions"))
        display(Markdown(
            "Distributions of transcripts, genes detected, cell area, and nucleus area "
            "across all cells in this sample, before any filtering. All four are on log "
            "axes; the red line marks each median. Cells at zero cannot be drawn on a "
            "log axis and are counted in the panel title instead."
        ))
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=FIGSIZE, squeeze=False)
        for ax, (col, label, log) in zip(axes.ravel(), QC_COLUMNS):
            log_hist(ax, obs[col], label, log)
        for ax in axes.ravel()[len(QC_COLUMNS):]:
            fig.delaxes(ax)
        fig.suptitle(f"{sample} · {len(obs):,} cells", fontsize=9, x=0.01, ha="left")
        fig.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
        plt.close(fig)

        # ── QC in tissue ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        display(Markdown("## QC in tissue coordinates"))
        display(Markdown(
            "Every cell at its position on the slide, coloured by transcript count on "
            "the left and by genes detected on the right, both on log colour scales. "
            "Axes are in µm and share an equal aspect, so the panels are at tissue "
            "proportions."
        ))
        fig, axes = tissue_figure(obs, 2)
        spatial_panels = [
            ("transcript_counts", "Transcripts"),
            ("n_genes_by_transcripts", "Genes"),
        ]
        for ax, (col, label) in zip(axes.ravel(), spatial_panels):
            values = obs[col].to_numpy(dtype=float)
            # LogNorm rejects a zero vmin, and both columns reach zero on real data.
            # Clipping the floor to 1 keeps those cells drawn at the bottom of the ramp
            # rather than dropping them from the panel that exists to locate them.
            im = ax.scatter(
                obs["spatial_x"], obs["spatial_y"],
                c=np.clip(values, 1, None),
                s=point_size(ax, len(obs)),
                cmap="viridis",
                norm=LogNorm(vmin=1, vmax=max(values.max(), 2)),
                linewidths=0,
            )
            ax.set_aspect("equal")
            # Slide y runs downward in Xenium's frame; inverting keeps the tissue the
            # way round it appears in Xenium Explorer.
            ax.invert_yaxis()
            ax.set_title(label, size=8)
            ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
            cbar = fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.046, pad=0.02)
            cbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
        fig.suptitle(f"{sample} · {len(obs):,} cells", fontsize=9, x=0.01, ha="left")
        fig.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
        plt.close(fig)

        # ── Cell retention ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
        display(Markdown("## Cells retained by transcript threshold"))
        display(Markdown(
            "Share of this sample's cells surviving a minimum-transcript cut, across a "
            "range of thresholds. The cut keeps cells at or above the threshold. The "
            f"dashed line marks the pipeline's current cut of {DEFAULT_MIN_COUNTS}. The "
            "table gives the retained cell count at selected thresholds."
        ))
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(FIGSIZE[0] * 0.62, FIGSIZE[1]))
        ax.plot(COUNT_GRID, 100 * cell_curve, marker="o", ms=3, color="#4C72B0")
        ax.axvline(DEFAULT_MIN_COUNTS, color="#555555", ls="--", lw=1)
        ax.set_xlabel("Minimum transcripts per cell", size=7)
        ax.set_ylabel("Cells retained (%)", size=7)
        ax.set_ylim(0, 101)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
        ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
        fig.suptitle(f"{sample} · {len(obs):,} cells", fontsize=9, x=0.01, ha="left")
        fig.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
        plt.close(fig)

        # Its own slide with its own heading, not a caption under the curve above.
        # Pandoc's pptx writer puts a table on a slide of its own no matter what, so
        # without a heading here the table lands on an untitled slide that takes its
        # title from the first header cell — "Min transcripts" as a slide title.
        display(Markdown("## Cells retained — selected thresholds"))
        display(Markdown(
            "Cell counts surviving a minimum-transcript cut at selected thresholds for "
            "this sample, as absolute counts and as a share of the unfiltered total."
        ))
        callouts = retained_fraction(counts, np.array(COUNT_CALLOUTS))
        table = ["| Min transcripts | Cells retained | % retained | Cells dropped |",
                 "|---:|---:|---:|---:|"]
        for threshold, frac in zip(COUNT_CALLOUTS, callouts):
            kept = int(round(frac * len(obs)))
            table.append(f"| {threshold} | {kept:,} | {100 * frac:.1f} | {len(obs) - kept:,} |")
        display(Markdown("\n".join(table)))

        # ── Controls and segmentation ────────────────────────────────────────
        display(Markdown("## Negative controls and segmentation"))
        display(Markdown(
            "Left: total transcripts assigned to each of the five Xenium control and "
            "codeword categories across the whole sample, on a log axis. Right: how many "
            "cells were segmented by each method. The subtitle gives the share of cells "
            "carrying at least one control transcript and the mean per-cell control "
            "fraction."
        ))
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=FIGSIZE, squeeze=False)
        ax = axes[0, 0]
        totals = obs[CONTROL_COLS].sum()
        # Horizontal bars: the category names are long enough that vertical ticks would
        # overlap or need rotating to fit.
        ax.barh(range(len(totals)), totals.to_numpy(), color="#C44E52")
        ax.set_yticks(range(len(totals)),
                      [c.replace("_counts", "").replace("_", " ") for c in totals.index],
                      fontsize=6)
        ax.set_xscale("log")
        ax.set_xlabel("Total transcripts (log)", size=7)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
        ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

        ax = axes[0, 1]
        seg = obs["segmentation_method"].value_counts()
        ax.barh(range(len(seg)), seg.to_numpy(), color="#4C72B0")
        # Long stain lists; truncate rather than let them consume the panel.
        ax.set_yticks(range(len(seg)),
                      [s if len(s) <= 34 else s[:31] + "…" for s in seg.index],
                      fontsize=6)
        # Log axis for the same reason the control panel uses one: nucleus-expansion and
        # the 0.25x boundary stain account for tens of cells against ~20,000 segmented by
        # interior stain, and on a linear axis their bars are literally invisible.
        ax.set_xscale("log")
        ax.set_xlabel("Cells (log)", size=7)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
        ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

        control_cells = 100 * (obs["control_counts"] > 0).mean()
        mean_pct = obs["pct_control"].mean()
        fig.suptitle(
            f"{sample} · {control_cells:.1f}% of cells carry a control · "
            f"mean control fraction {mean_pct:.3f}%",
            fontsize=9, x=0.01, ha="left",
        )
        fig.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
        plt.close(fig)

        # ── Gene detection ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
        display(Markdown("## Gene detection and the min_cells cut"))
        display(Markdown(
            "Left: how many cells each panel gene is detected in, on a log axis. Right: "
            "share of the panel surviving a minimum-cells cut. The dashed line marks the "
            f"pipeline's current cut of {DEFAULT_MIN_CELLS}. The subtitle gives the panel "
            "size and how many genes are detected in no cells at all."
        ))
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=FIGSIZE, squeeze=False)
        log_hist(axes[0, 0], gene_cells, "Cells per gene", True)
        axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("Genes", size=7)
        ax = axes[0, 1]
        ax.plot(CELL_GRID, 100 * gene_curve, marker="o", ms=3, color="#4C72B0")
        ax.axvline(DEFAULT_MIN_CELLS, color="#555555", ls="--", lw=1)
        ax.set_xlabel("Minimum cells per gene", size=7)
        ax.set_ylabel("Panel retained (%)", size=7)
        ax.set_ylim(0, 101)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
        ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
        n_absent = int((gene_cells == 0).sum())
        fig.suptitle(
            f"{sample} · {len(var):,} genes · {n_absent:,} detected in no cells",
            fontsize=9, x=0.01, ha="left",
        )
        fig.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
        plt.close(fig)

        # Carried to the cohort section. Only the summary scalars and the two curves are
        # kept; the obs frame itself is dropped with the sample.
        summaries.append({
            "sample": sample,
            "cells": len(obs),
            "genes": len(var),
            "median_transcripts": float(np.median(counts)),
            "median_genes": float(obs["n_genes_by_transcripts"].median()),
            "median_cell_area": float(obs["cell_area"].median()),
            "pct_control": float(mean_pct),
            "genes_absent": n_absent,
            "pct_cells_at_default": 100 * float(
                retained_fraction(counts, np.array([DEFAULT_MIN_COUNTS]))[0]),
            "pct_genes_at_default": 100 * float(
                retained_fraction(gene_cells, np.array([DEFAULT_MIN_CELLS]))[0]),
        })
        curves[sample] = (cell_curve, gene_curve)
        distributions[sample] = {
            col: obs[col].to_numpy(dtype=float) for col, _, _ in QC_COLUMNS
        }
    except Exception:
        display(Markdown(f"```\n{traceback.format_exc()}\n```"))

    del obs, var
```

```{python}
# The cohort section comes last, after every per-sample section, so the overlays are read
# against samples the reader has already seen individually — and so a sample that failed
# above is simply absent from them rather than breaking them.
if summaries:
    summary = pd.DataFrame(summaries).sort_values("sample").reset_index(drop=True)
    samples = list(summary["sample"])
    colors = dict(zip(samples, sample_colors(len(samples))))

    display(Markdown("# Cohort"))

    # ── Summary table ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    display(Markdown("## Cohort summary"))
    display(Markdown(
        "One row per sample: cell and panel counts before filtering, median per-cell QC, "
        "mean per-cell negative-control fraction, and the share of cells and genes that "
        f"survive the pipeline's current cuts of {DEFAULT_MIN_COUNTS} transcripts per "
        f"cell and {DEFAULT_MIN_CELLS} cells per gene."
    ))
    header = ["| Sample | Cells | Median tx | Median genes | Median area (µm²) "
              "| Control % | Genes absent | Cells kept % | Genes kept % |",
              "|:--|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|"]
    for row in summary.itertuples():
        header.append(
            f"| {row.sample} | {row.cells:,} | {row.median_transcripts:,.0f} "
            f"| {row.median_genes:,.0f} | {row.median_cell_area:,.0f} "
            f"| {row.pct_control:.3f} | {row.genes_absent:,} "
            f"| {row.pct_cells_at_default:.1f} | {row.pct_genes_at_default:.1f} |"
        )
    display(Markdown("\n".join(header)))

    # ── Distributions across samples ─────────────────────────────────────────
    display(Markdown("## Per-cell QC across samples"))
    display(Markdown(
        "Cumulative distributions of the per-cell QC metrics, one line per sample, on log "
        "axes. Each curve gives the share of that sample's cells at or below a given "
        "value, so a curve lying to the left of the others is a sample with "
        "systematically lower values."
    ))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=FIGSIZE, squeeze=False)
    for ax, (col, label, log) in zip(axes.ravel(), QC_COLUMNS):
        for sample in samples:
            # A sample whose section raised above never reached `distributions`, so the
            # cohort panels simply omit it rather than failing on the lookup.
            values = distributions.get(sample, {}).get(col)
            if values is None:
                continue
            # ECDF rather than overlaid histograms: at eight samples the histograms
            # occlude each other, while the cumulative curves stay separable — and a
            # threshold reads off directly as the height of each curve at that x.
            ordered = np.sort(values[values > 0]) if log else np.sort(values)
            ax.plot(ordered, 100 * np.arange(1, len(ordered) + 1) / len(ordered),
                    lw=1.2, color=colors[sample], label=sample)
        if log:
            ax.set_xscale("log")
        ax.set_xlabel(label, size=7)
        ax.set_ylabel("Cells at or below (%)", size=7)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
        ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    for ax in axes.ravel()[len(QC_COLUMNS):]:
        fig.delaxes(ax)
    # One shared legend rather than one per panel: the sample colours are the same in
    # all four, and four legends would cost more panel area than the curves use.
    handles, labels = axes[0, 0].get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(handles, labels, loc="lower center", ncol=min(len(samples), 6), fontsize=6,
               frameon=False, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.02))
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)

    # ── Retention across samples ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    display(Markdown("## Retention across samples"))
    display(Markdown(
        "Share of cells surviving each minimum-transcript cut (left) and share of the "
        "panel surviving each minimum-cells cut (right), one line per sample. Dashed "
        f"lines mark the pipeline's current cuts of {DEFAULT_MIN_COUNTS} and "
        f"{DEFAULT_MIN_CELLS}. Both cuts keep at or above the threshold."
    ))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=FIGSIZE, squeeze=False)
    panels = [
        (axes[0, 0], COUNT_GRID, 0, DEFAULT_MIN_COUNTS,
         "Minimum transcripts per cell", "Cells retained (%)"),
        (axes[0, 1], CELL_GRID, 1, DEFAULT_MIN_CELLS,
         "Minimum cells per gene", "Panel retained (%)"),
    ]
    for ax, grid, index, default, xlabel, ylabel in panels:
        for sample in samples:
            ax.plot(grid, 100 * curves[sample][index], marker="o", ms=2.5, lw=1.2,
                    color=colors[sample], label=sample)
        ax.axvline(default, color="#555555", ls="--", lw=1)
        ax.set_xlabel(xlabel, size=7)
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, size=7)
        ax.set_ylim(0, 101)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
        ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    handles, labels = axes[0, 0].get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(handles, labels, loc="lower center", ncol=min(len(samples), 6), fontsize=6,
               frameon=False, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.02))
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)

    # ── Threshold handoff ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Written pre-filled with the DEFAULTS, not with anything inferred from the curves
    # above. Picking a threshold is a judgement made by reading these slides, and a deck
    # that guessed one would put a number nobody chose into a file that looks decided.
    # What this file saves is the typing and the sample-name spelling; the values are
    # meant to be edited before it is passed back via --thresholds.
    thresholds = pd.DataFrame({
        "sample": samples,
        "min_counts": DEFAULT_MIN_COUNTS,
        "min_cells": DEFAULT_MIN_CELLS,
    })
    thresholds.to_csv("qc_thresholds.csv", index=False)
else:
    # An empty deck still has to produce the file the process declares as an output, or
    # the task fails on a missing path rather than on whatever actually went wrong.
    pd.DataFrame(columns=["sample", "min_counts", "min_cells"]).to_csv(
        "qc_thresholds.csv", index=False)
```
